main_text.p: Παγιδεύω illaqueo, irretio. Fut. εύσω. P. πεπα- γιδευμαι.
Πάθος, εος, τὸ affectus Roman.1.v.26. morbus 1.Thess.4.5. mollities Col.3.5.
Πάθημα, τος, τὸ afflictio, Rom.8.18. vitiosus affectus Gal.5.24. à πάσχω patior.
Παθητὸς, ἡ, ὁ proprie, passibilis, qui pati potest.
Παῖς, παιδὸς, ὁ, ἡ puer, puella. per Hebraismum servus Act.4.27.

Παιδεύω erudio, castigo. imperf. ἐπαίδευον. Fut. εύσω. P. πεπαίδευμαι. aor.1. ἐπαίδευσα. praef. pass. παιδεύομαι castigor. prat. pass. πεπαίδευμαι. part. πεπαιδευμένος instítutus. aor.1. pass. ἐπαιδεύθην, ης, η. aor.1. pass. subj. παιδευθῶ, ης, η.
Παιδαγωγὸς, ἐ, ὁ paedagogus, puerorum dux, custos, informator. ex παῖς puer & ἀγωγὸς, ὁ dux. Th. ἀγω duco.
Παιδίον, ἐ, τὸ infans, puerulus. diminutivum à παῖς, δὸς, ὁ puer.
Παιδιόθεν ab incunabulis, ab ineunte aetate, seu, à pueritia, Adv.
Παιδίσκη, ης, ἡ ancilla. παιδίσκος, ἐ, ὁ puellus. diminutivum à nomine παῖς puer.
Παίζω (contracte pro παιδίζω, more puerorum lusito) ludo, salto, 1.Cor.10.7. F. παίξω. P. πεπαιγμαι. a.1. ἐπαιξα, Jud.16.26.

page.notes: The right-hand margin notes are cut and largely illegible; only fragments such as "Adverb. olim", "antiquo", "lucta, Ethe", "generatio" are discernible, so they are not transcribed. Greek accents and breathings in the headwords are reproduced approximately; several Greek forms in the scan are partly smudged and should be checked against the original.
